MCPSense Static Analysis Security and Bug Scan Report

Report Timestamp: 2024-06-02T

Target: MCPSense Project

SUMMARY:
---------
Total Findings: 5
Categories: spec-compliance (1), security (4)
Severity Levels: critical (2), high (1), medium (1), low (1)

DETAILED FINDINGS:
------------------

1) ID: SEC-002
   Title: Command Injection via Untrusted Shell Input
   Severity: critical
   Category: security
   Location: testdata/vulnerable_server/server.go, lines ~24
   Description: RunCommand uses exec.Command with shell "sh -c" to run user-provided input without sanitization or validation.
   This allows arbitrary command injection executing injected shell commands, a serious vulnerability.
   Remediation: Avoid using shell command invocation that interprets strings. Use exec.Command with arguments separated and sanitized.

2) ID: SEC-003
   Title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Risk
   Severity: high
   Category: security
   Location: testdata/vulnerable_server/server.go, lines ~43
   Description: FetchURL performs HTTP GET on arbitrary user-supplied URLs without allowlisting or validation.
   This enables SSRF attacks targeting internal or private network resources.
   Remediation: Implement strong allowlist validation for domains and protocols before issuing HTTP requests.

3) ID: SEC-004
   Title: Path Traversal and Arbitrary File Reads
   Severity: critical
   Category: security
   Location: testdata/vulnerable_server/server.go, lines ~54
   Description: ReadFile reads file paths directly from user input without sanitizing or restricting file system boundaries.
   Allows path traversal attacks and leakage of sensitive system files.
   Remediation: Implement filepath sanitization and restrict path access to predefined safe directories.

4) ID: SEC-007
   Title: Unsafe Command String Formatting
   Severity: medium
   Category: security
   Location: testdata/vulnerable_server/server.go, lines ~34
   Description: RunCommandSprintf calls fmt.Sprintf to build shell command strings with user inputs directly injected.
   This leads to shell injection risks similar to SEC-002.
   Remediation: Avoid string formatting commands with untrusted user input. Use exec.Command argument array instead.

5) ID: SPEC-001
   Title: Missing Manifest File or Invalid Manifest Parsing
   Severity: low
   Category: spec-compliance
   Location: internal/scanner/static.go
   Description: The static scanner tries multiple locations and attempts to parse manifests, but does not return an error
   if no valid manifest is found. This could cause silent failures during scans.
   Remediation: Consider returning an explicit error or warning when no valid manifest is found to improve reliability.


SUMMARY OF GOOD PRACTICES FOUND:
--------------------------------
- CLI and JSON reporters are cleanly separated with interfaces, allowing extensible output formats.
- Severity scoring system assigns numeric scores for risk quantification.
- Logger supports multiple log levels and flexible output writers.
- Compliant server example shows domain allowlisting, path sanitization, and avoiding shell command injection.
